description: Run your Capacitor, Flutter, React Native and Electron apps on iPhone simulators, iPhones, the Mac and Windows, straight from VS Code. With a paired Mac, or no Mac at all
untrusted: CapMac builds and runs your project's code, so it needs a trusted folder
welcome.noFolder:
Open the folder of your Capacitor, Flutter, React Native or Electron app. CapMac finds the app in it.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)
New here? Try a sample app.
[Try a sample app](command:capmac.trySample)
welcome.noApp:
CapMac found no app it can run in this folder. It runs Capacitor, Ionic, Flutter, React Native and Electron apps.
[Look again](command:capmac.refresh)
[Try a sample app](command:capmac.trySample)
[Get started](command:capmac.getStarted)
welcome.noAppFolders:
CapMac found no app it can run in these folders. It runs Capacitor, Ionic, Flutter, React Native and Electron apps.
[Look again](command:capmac.refresh)
[Try a sample app](command:capmac.trySample)
[Get started](command:capmac.getStarted)
welcome.apps:
No apps found yet. Open the folder with your capacitor.config file, your Flutter app's pubspec.yaml, or your React Native or Electron app's package.json.
[Look again](command:capmac.refresh)
welcome.devices:
Pair your Mac to run your app on its iPhone and iPad simulators, on iPhones plugged into it, and on its desktop.
[Pair a Mac](command:capmac.pairMac)

debug.mode: live: keep the app running and reload it when you save. run: build and open it once
debug.mode.run: Build and open the app once
debug.mode.live: Keep it running and reload it when you save (hot reload for Flutter)
debug.projectPath: The project folder (the one with capacitor.config, pubspec.yaml or the Electron app's package.json)
debug.app: Which of the project's apps: ios, electron, or a Flutter or React Native app's macos or windows. Leave it out for the one picked in CapMac
debug.target: Where it runs: a simulator's or iPhone's name or UDID. Leave it out for the one picked in CapMac
debug.mac: The paired Mac to use, by name. Leave it out for the default
debug.backend.wsl: On this PC, with no Mac (runs on an iPhone plugged into this PC)
debug.webBuild: Build the web app first (Capacitor). false uses the files built last time
debug.configuration: The Xcode build configuration (Debug, Release, …). Release runs a React Native app as people get it, its JavaScript inside
debug.flutterMode: A Flutter app's mode for Run: debug, profile or release
debug.screen: Open the live screen when the app starts
debug.snippet.live: Run with live reload on the simulator or device picked in CapMac
debug.snippet.target: Run on a simulator, by its name
cfg.screen.openOnRun: Open the live screen when a run starts
cfg.screen.openOnRun.auto: For simulators and Mac apps (a real iPhone shows itself)
cfg.screen.openOnRun.always: Whenever the app has a screen CapMac can show
cfg.screen.location.window: In a window of its own, like a real simulator
cfg.screen.deviceFrame: Draw a phone outline around simulators, and a title bar on Mac app windows
cfg.console.buildSteps: Show each build step in the Debug Console
cfg.console.bridge: Show Capacitor's bridge messages (between the web view and native code) in the Debug Console
cfg.osLogs: Show the iPhone's system logs (NSLog and os_log) next to your app's console
cfg.verbose: Show every line the build tools print (for troubleshooting)
cfg.packageWarnings: Show warnings from Pods, Swift packages and `node_modules` in Problems
cfg.codeLens: Show Run and Live above capacitor.config, pubspec.yaml and capmac.json
cfg.terminal.capmacCommand: Add the `capmac` command to VS Code's terminals and to the AI agents VS Code starts (like the Claude Code and Codex panels), when it isn't installed already
cfg.agents.addSkill: Add CapMac's skill by itself, so AI agents (Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and others) know how to run and check your app. CapMac asks before it replaces a skill that is already there. **CapMac: Add the CapMac Skill for AI Agents…** adds it again
cfg.agents.addSkill.project: In each project with an app, the first time CapMac opens it. Commit it so your team's agents get it too
cfg.agents.addSkill.global: Once, for all your projects, in each agent's folder in your user profile
cfg.agents.addSkill.off: Only when you add it yourself
walk.title: Get started with CapMac
walk.description: Run your app on an iPhone simulator, an iPhone, the Mac or Windows, right from VS Code
walk.where.title: Choose where your app builds
walk.where.description:
Pair your Mac to use its simulators and the iPhones plugged into it. No Mac? This PC can build your iPhone app and put it on an iPhone plugged in with a cable.
[Pair a Mac](command:capmac.pairMac)
[Set up this PC (no Mac)](command:capmac.setupPc)
walk.app.title: Open your app
walk.app.description:
Open the folder of your Capacitor, Flutter, React Native or Electron app. CapMac finds its apps: the iPhone app, the Electron app, a Flutter or React Native app's Mac and Windows apps.
[Open Folder](command:workbench.action.files.openFolder)
[Try a sample app](command:capmac.trySample)
walk.run.title: Run it, with live reload
walk.run.description:
Live builds and opens your app, then updates it when you save (Flutter hot-reloads). Its console shows in the Debug Console, its build errors in Problems. Every run is a debug session: pick Live in Run and Debug once and F5 does it.
[Run with Live Reload](command:capmac.live)
walk.screen.title: See it and use it, in VS Code
walk.screen.description:
The simulator's screen, or the Mac app's window, in a tab beside your code: click, scroll and type on it.
[Show the Screen](command:capmac.showScreen)
walk.ai.title: Let your AI agent run the app
walk.ai.description:
In Copilot's agent mode, CapMac's tools let the agent run your app, read its console and look at its screen. Ask: “run my app and check the login screen”
Claude Code, Codex, Gemini CLI and other agents learn the `capmac` command from CapMac's skill. CapMac adds it to your project for the agents it finds.
[Add the CapMac skill](command:capmac.addSkill)
